name: PlantUML Interactive Desktop Editor
description: Intent architecture for porting the PlantUML Interactive Editor web app to a Windows desktop application with drag-and-drop editing, free-form canvas positioning, and one-click export.

elements.name: SystemArchitecture
elements.description: Top-level architecture grouping for the PlantUML Desktop Editor

elements.name: Deliver PlantUML Desktop Editor
elements.description: Transform existing web-based PlantUML Interactive Editor into a self-contained Windows desktop application with drag-and-drop editing

testcases.name: TC-GOAL-1
testcases.description: Goal: Transform web-based PlantUML Interactive Editor into self-contained Windows desktop app with drag-and-drop
testcases.Input: Complete application build; verify no browser or server required for editing
testcases.controlPoint: Complete application build; verify no browser or server required for editing

elements.name: Developer need for intuitive PlantUML editing on Windows
elements.description: Developers want a visual interactive tool to create PlantUML diagrams without learning PlantUML syntax

testcases.name: TC-DRIVER-NEED-1
testcases.description: Driver: Developer need for intuitive PlantUML editing on Windows 鈥?developers create a complete Activity Diagram without writing PlantUML syntax manually
testcases.Input: First-time developer uses the application to create an Activity Diagram with at least 5 nodes, branching, and connections
testcases.controlPoint: First-time developer uses the application to create an Activity Diagram with at least 5 nodes, branching, and connections

elements.name: Zero-configuration setup requirement
elements.description: Users expect to install with defaults and start immediately, without Python, Java, or environment variable setup

testcases.name: TC-DRIVER-ZERO-1
testcases.description: Driver: Zero-configuration setup requirement 鈥?application works immediately after install with no manual runtime setup
testcases.Input: Clean Windows 10/11 VM. Download installer, install with default settings, launch application
testcases.controlPoint: Clean Windows 10/11 VM. Download installer, install with default settings, launch application

elements.name: Assessment: Current web app friction
elements.description: Current web app requires Python, Java, PlantUML JAR download, .env configuration, and browser launch. High setup friction limits adoption.

testcases.name: TC-ASSESS-1
testcases.description: Assessment: Current web app friction resolved 鈥?desktop app eliminates the specific friction points: no Python setup, no Java setup, no .env configuration, no browser launch
testcases.Input: Audit the delivered desktop application against the five identified friction points from the web app
testcases.controlPoint: Audit the delivered desktop application against the five identified friction points from the web app

elements.name: Principle: Single-click zero-config installer
elements.description: Application MUST be installable by clicking Next-Next-Finish. All dependencies handled automatically on first launch.

testcases.name: TC-PRINC-INSTALL-1
testcases.description: Principle: Single-click zero-config installer 鈥?application MUST be installable by clicking Next-Next-Finish
testcases.Input: Run NSIS installer on a clean Windows 10/11 PC
testcases.controlPoint: Run NSIS installer on a clean Windows 10/11 PC

elements.name: Principle: Free-form canvas positioning
elements.description: Users can freely position elements anywhere via drag-and-drop. PlantUML auto-layout NOT used for editing. .puml export contains structure only.

testcases.name: TC-PRINC-FREEFORM-1
testcases.description: Principle: Free-form canvas positioning 鈥?users can freely position elements anywhere via drag-and-drop; .puml export contains logical structure only, no positional data
testcases.Input: Drag multiple elements to arbitrary positions on canvas; export to .puml
testcases.controlPoint: Drag multiple elements to arbitrary positions on canvas; export to .puml

elements.name: Principle: Last-write-wins bidirectional sync
elements.description: Canvas and code editor synced bidirectionally. Last modification by timestamp wins and regenerates the other.

testcases.name: TC-PRINC-SYNC-1
testcases.description: Principle: Last-write-wins bidirectional sync 鈥?canvas and code editor synced bidirectionally; last modification by timestamp wins
testcases.Input: Edit canvas by moving a node, then immediately edit code by typing. Observe sync behavior.
testcases.controlPoint: Edit canvas by moving a node, then immediately edit code by typing. Observe sync behavior.

elements.name: Requirement: Drag-and-drop Activity Diagram editing
elements.description: Users can drag elements from a palette onto a canvas and position them freely. All three levels must be supported: A) add from palette, B) reorder/move on canvas, C) reconnect arrows.

testcases.name: TC-REQ-DD-1
testcases.description: Requirement: Users can drag elements from palette onto canvas and position them freely. All three levels (add, reposition, reconnect) are supported.
testcases.Input: Open app, drag Activity from palette to canvas, drag existing node to new position, drag connector handle from node A to node B
testcases.controlPoint: Open app, drag Activity from palette to canvas, drag existing node to new position, drag connector handle from node A to node B

elements.name: Requirement: One-click export to .puml and .png
elements.description: Users can export diagrams with a single click. .puml export contains logical structure only. .png export renders via PlantUML.

testcases.name: TC-REQ-EX-1
testcases.description: Requirement: One-click export to .puml (logical structure only) and .png (rendered via PlantUML)
testcases.Input: File鈫扙xport鈫?puml, File鈫扙xport鈫?png
testcases.controlPoint: File鈫扙xport鈫?puml, File鈫扙xport鈫?png

elements.name: Requirement: Import existing .puml files
elements.description: Users can open existing .puml files. Parser reconstructs AST from text and lays out elements on a default grid for further editing.

testcases.name: TC-REQ-IM-1
testcases.description: Requirement: Import existing .puml files 鈥?parser reconstructs AST and lays out elements on a default grid for editing
testcases.Input: File鈫扥pen鈫抯elect .puml file with Activity Diagram content
testcases.controlPoint: File鈫扥pen鈫抯elect .puml file with Activity Diagram content

elements.name: Requirement: Bidirectional canvas-code synchronization
elements.description: Canvas edits update code editor, code editor edits update canvas. Last-write-wins conflict resolution. Fingerprint matching preserves element positions across re-parses.

testcases.name: TC-REQ-SYNC-1
testcases.description: Requirement: Bidirectional canvas-code sync with last-write-wins conflict resolution and 200ms debounce
testcases.Input: Edit canvas (dray node), observe code editor updates. Edit code, observe canvas updates. Make simultaneous edits.
testcases.controlPoint: Edit canvas (dray node), observe code editor updates. Edit code, observe canvas updates. Make simultaneous edits.

elements.name: Constraint: Electron + React + TypeScript stack
elements.description: Desktop application built with Electron shell, React with TypeScript, Vite build tool. ReactFlow for canvas. Ace Editor for code.

testcases.name: TC-CONST-ELECTRON-1
testcases.description: Constraint: Desktop app built with Electron + React + TypeScript + Vite stack
testcases.Input: Inspect package.json, tsconfig, and build scripts
testcases.controlPoint: Inspect package.json, tsconfig, and build scripts

elements.name: Constraint: Windows-only desktop application
elements.description: Target platform is Windows 10/11 64-bit. Installer via electron-builder + NSIS. No cross-platform requirement for MVP.

testcases.name: TC-CONST-WIN-1
testcases.description: Constraint: Windows-only (10/11 64-bit) with NSIS installer via electron-builder
testcases.Input: Build installer on Windows; install on clean Windows 10/11 VM
testcases.controlPoint: Build installer on Windows; install on clean Windows 10/11 VM

elements.name: Constraint: Python backend minimal footprint
elements.description: Python backend retained ONLY for PlantUML rendering API (SVG/PNG generation via Java subprocess). All ~40 existing PlantUML manipulation endpoints replaced by TypeScript AST.

testcases.name: TC-CONST-PY-1
testcases.description: Constraint: Python backend retained ONLY for render endpoints; all ~40 manipulation endpoints replaced by TypeScript AST
testcases.Input: Inspect Python backend source; compare endpoints with architecture intent
testcases.controlPoint: Inspect Python backend source; compare endpoints with architecture intent

elements.name: Outcome: Developers create PlantUML diagrams via drag-and-drop on Windows
elements.description: Users install the desktop app once, drag-and-drop to create/edit PlantUML activity diagrams, export .puml and .png, without any manual environment setup.

testcases.name: TC-OUTCOME-1
testcases.description: Outcome: Developers create/edit PlantUML activity diagrams via drag-and-drop and export .puml/.png without manual environment setup
testcases.Input: First-time user installs and uses the application end-to-end
testcases.controlPoint: First-time user installs and uses the application end-to-end

elements.name: Concern A: AST Data Model
elements.description: Defines all TypeScript types for PlantUML activity diagram elements (ActivityNode, IfNode, WhileNode, ForkNode, SwitchNode, etc.), ContainerNode abstraction, DiagramModel, and EdgeData. Foundation for all other concerns.

testcases.name: TC-AST-1
testcases.description: AST Data Model defines all TypeScript types for PlantUML Activity Diagram elements (ActivityNode, IfNode, WhileNode, ForkNode, SwitchNode, ContainerNode, DiagramModel, EdgeData) and they compile without type errors
testcases.Input: TypeScript compiler checks all AST type definitions in the model module
testcases.controlPoint: TypeScript compiler checks all AST type definitions in the model module

testcases.name: TC-AST-2
testcases.description: AST Data Model supports serialization/deserialization to/from JSON for save/load round-trip
testcases.Input: Create a DiagramModel instance with nested containers and edges, serialize to JSON, deserialize back
testcases.controlPoint: Create a DiagramModel instance with nested containers and edges, serialize to JSON, deserialize back

elements.name: Concern B: ReactFlow Canvas Engine
elements.description: ReactFlow-based free-form canvas with custom node renderers for each PlantUML element type. Handles drag-and-drop, free positioning, connection handles, container nesting visualization.

testcases.name: TC-B-1
testcases.description: ReactFlow Canvas renders custom node types for each PlantUML element (StartNode, StopNode, ActivityNode, IfNode, WhileNode, ForkNode, SwitchNode) on a free-form canvas
testcases.Input: Initialize ReactFlow with a DiagramModel containing one node of each type
testcases.controlPoint: Initialize ReactFlow with a DiagramModel containing one node of each type

testcases.name: TC-B-2
testcases.description: Canvas supports all 3 drag-and-drop levels: A) palette to canvas, B) reposition on canvas, C) connector handle to create edge
testcases.Input: A) Drag from palette onto empty canvas. B) Drag existing node to new position. C) Drag connector handle from node A to node B.
testcases.controlPoint: A) Drag from palette onto empty canvas. B) Drag existing node to new position. C) Drag connector handle from node A to node B.

elements.name: Concern C: Ace Code Editor Wrapper
elements.description: Wraps Ace Editor with PlantUML syntax highlighting, line markers for canvas-code correspondence, and keyboard shortcuts. Provides the code editing modality.

testcases.name: TC-C-1
testcases.description: Ace Editor wrapper displays PlantUML code with syntax highlighting for Activity Diagram keywords (@startuml, @enduml, :Activity, if/else/endif, while/endwhile, fork/endfork, split/endsplit)
testcases.Input: Load a .puml Activity Diagram file into the Ace Editor
testcases.controlPoint: Load a .puml Activity Diagram file into the Ace Editor

testcases.name: TC-C-2
testcases.description: Code editor change events are emitted with debounce for bidirectional sync
testcases.Input: Type in Ace Editor; observe event emission timing
testcases.controlPoint: Type in Ace Editor; observe event emission timing

elements.name: Concern D: Bidirectional Sync Engine
elements.description: Manages canvas鈫攃ode synchronization with version numbers and timestamps. Implements last-write-wins conflict resolution. Maintains position-preserving fingerprint matching across re-parses.

testcases.name: TC-D-1
testcases.description: Bidirectional Sync applies last-write-wins: the last modification (by timestamp) between canvas and code wins and regenerates the other
testcases.Input: Make a canvas edit, then within the 200ms debounce window make a code edit. Wait for sync.
testcases.controlPoint: Make a canvas edit, then within the 200ms debounce window make a code edit. Wait for sync.

testcases.name: TC-D-2
testcases.description: Fingerprint matching preserves element positions across re-parses when importing/re-opening .puml files
testcases.Input: Edit a diagram, export to .puml, re-import the .puml file
testcases.controlPoint: Edit a diagram, export to .puml, re-import the .puml file

elements.name: Concern E: PlantUML Parser and Generator
elements.description: Parser: PlantUML text to AST with stack-based nesting tracking and forward/backward scanning for block boundaries. Generator: AST to PlantUML text with depth-tracked indentation. Both include tolerance for unsupported/partially-parsed elements.

testcases.name: TC-E-1
testcases.description: Parser correctly converts Activity Diagram PlantUML text to AST with stack-based nesting tracking for if/while/fork containers

testcases.name: TC-E-2
testcases.description: Generator converts AST back to valid PlantUML text with depth-tracked indentation
testcases.Input: Take a parsed AST, generate PlantUML text, re-parse the generated text
testcases.controlPoint: Take a parsed AST, generate PlantUML text, re-parse the generated text

elements.name: Concern F: Component Palette
elements.description: Left-panel draggable element palette. Categories: Flow (Activity, Start, Stop, Connector), Structure (If, While, Fork, Switch), Decoration (Note, Group, Title). Drag preview and snap-zone indicators.

testcases.name: TC-F-1
testcases.description: Component Palette displays draggable element categories: Flow (Activity, Start, Stop, Connector), Structure (If, While, Fork, Switch), Decoration (Note, Group, Title)
testcases.Input: Open the application; inspect the left-panel palette
testcases.controlPoint: Open the application; inspect the left-panel palette

testcases.name: TC-F-2
testcases.description: Dragging an item from palette to canvas creates a new element of the correct type at the drop position
testcases.Input: Drag 'Activity' from palette to canvas at position (200, 300)
testcases.controlPoint: Drag 'Activity' from palette to canvas at position (200, 300)

elements.name: Concern G: Electron Desktop Shell
elements.description: Electron main process: window management, native menus (File/Edit/Help), file dialogs for import/export, subprocess management for Python backend, JRE download on first launch, auto-updater.

testcases.name: TC-G-1
testcases.description: Electron Desktop Shell provides native menus: File (Open, Export .puml, Export .png, Exit), Edit (Undo, Redo), Help (About)
testcases.Input: Click each menu item in the application window
testcases.controlPoint: Click each menu item in the application window

testcases.name: TC-G-2
testcases.description: Electron manages Python render backend subprocess lifecycle: spawn on first export, health-check polling, graceful shutdown
testcases.Input: Trigger first .png export; close application
testcases.controlPoint: Trigger first .png export; close application

elements.name: Electron
elements.description: Desktop application shell providing Chromium renderer, Node.js main process, native APIs (file dialogs, menus, subprocess management)

testcases.name: TC-TECH-ELECTRON-1
testcases.description: Electron provides Chromium renderer, Node.js main process, and native APIs (file dialogs, menus, subprocess)
testcases.Input: Start the application; verify Electron runtime
testcases.controlPoint: Start the application; verify Electron runtime

elements.name: React + TypeScript + Vite
elements.description: UI framework (React 18+), type-safe language (TypeScript), and build tool (Vite) for the renderer process

testcases.name: TC-TECH-REACT-1
testcases.description: React 18+ with TypeScript strict mode and Vite build tool
testcases.Input: Build the application; verify TypeScript compilation
testcases.controlPoint: Build the application; verify TypeScript compilation

elements.name: ReactFlow
elements.description: Node-based canvas library for interactive diagram editing with custom node types, edge types, connection handles, and group/container support

testcases.name: TC-TECH-RF-1
testcases.description: ReactFlow provides node-based canvas with custom node/edge types, connection handles, and group/container support
testcases.Input: Initialize ReactFlow with custom node types defined by Concern A AST
testcases.controlPoint: Initialize ReactFlow with custom node types defined by Concern A AST

elements.name: Ace Editor
elements.description: Browser-based code editor with PlantUML syntax highlighting, line markers, and keyboard shortcut customization

testcases.name: TC-TECH-ACE-1
testcases.description: Ace Editor with PlantUML syntax highlighting, line markers, and keyboard shortcuts
testcases.Input: Open a .puml file in Ace Editor
testcases.controlPoint: Open a .puml file in Ace Editor

elements.name: Node.js
elements.description: JavaScript runtime for Electron main process and npm package management

testcases.name: TC-TECH-NODE-1
testcases.description: Node.js runtime for Electron main process and npm package management
testcases.Input: Verify Node.js runtime availability
testcases.controlPoint: Verify Node.js runtime availability

elements.name: JRE (jlink minimal)
elements.description: Minimal Java runtime (~40MB) generated by jlink containing only java.base and java.xml modules. Downloaded on first launch.

testcases.description: JRE (jlink minimal, ~40MB) downloaded on first launch with progress indicator

elements.name: Python Render Backend (PyInstaller)
elements.description: PyInstaller-packaged Python Flask app retaining only the /render (SVG) and /renderPNG (PNG) endpoints. Spawned as subprocess by Electron. Uses JRE + plantuml.jar for rendering.

testcases.name: TC-TECH-PY-1

testcases.controlPoint: Start Python backend; call /render and /renderPNG endpoints

testcases.Input: First launch without plantuml.jar; trigger .png export
testcases.controlPoint: First launch without plantuml.jar; trigger .png export
